rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's closing transmission machinery. Both letters ask the recipient to lay attached legislation before the appropriate chamber and immediately state that a parallel draft was transmitted to the presiding officer of the other chamber, using parenthetical alternatives for the paired versions. This distinctive two-sentence formula is materially closer than generic bill-transmittal language. C05 shares part of the first sentence but lacks the complete reciprocal-transmission formula; C16 has a parallel-recipient notice but substantially different wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am transmitting herewith a draft of a proposed bill
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am transmitting herewith a draft of legislation
shared_material.explanation: Both open by transmitting draft legislation, though this language alone is routine.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It would be appreciated if you would lay the proposed bill before the Senate (House of Representatives).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I will appreciate it if you will lay the draft legislation before the House of Representatives (the Senate).
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively close request language, with the chamber alternatives reversed to accommodate paired letters.

shared_material.child_excerpt: A similar proposed bill has been transmitted to the Speaker of the House of Representatives (President of the Senate).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A similar draft has been transmitted to the President of the Senate (the Speaker of the House of Representatives).
shared_material.explanation: The same reciprocal-transmission sentence follows immediately, naming the corresponding presiding officers through parenthetical alternatives.
